Under Wine a program that reads what another process wrote needs the owner's message loop to run (a reader in another process waited until the owner's loop turned; in Windows the data is complete in the system once `SetClipboardData` returns), so the Wine tests keep the loop of the writer going while the other process reads. *Not done:* rendering the data on demand (`WM_RENDERFORMAT`: the app's own data is always complete), `CF_BITMAP`, HTML and RTF, `CF_TEXT` and `CF_OEMTEXT` (the system makes them from `CF_UNICODETEXT`), a limit on the size of a copy, and the change notification (`AddClipboardFormatListener`). *Tests.* Plain Go, with a fake `clipboardAPI`: the conversions of text (line breaks, NUL, surrogates), the URI and path rules, `DROPFILES` written and read (several paths, a network path, ANSI, damaged), the image round trip and the bitmaps of other programs (24 and 8 bits, 32 bits without alpha), a content written and read in every format, the retry (free, busy twice, busy nine times, busy for ever), a failure that is not busy, a failed set that closes the clipboard, `asyncRead` (the result on the UI thread, an ended context, an end while the thread works, once); under Wine, the real clipboard: a round trip of text, text with line breaks, files and an image, and all together; the formats on the clipboard (`\r\n`, `CF_HDROP`, `CF_DIBV5`, `PNG`); a second window of the process and a second process (this test binary started again, `TestWineClipboardHelper`) as the other program, reading and writing; a clipboard held by another thread that lets go during the third wait (the platform's `sleep` is replaced by the test), and one held for ever (`ClipboardBusy` after nine waits, for a write and for a read); a read of data that a process renders on demand and never answers, ended by its context; and the keys of `examples/editor` (Control+C, X and V, typed, copied, moved and pasted, compared pixel for pixel with an editor that starts with the result, each script ending with Control+A because a blinking caret shows at a different phase in the two frames).

### 25.8 Settings, fonts and lifecycle

Port from `settings_plugin.cc`, `system_utils.cc` and `windows_lifecycle_manager.cc`.

- **Settings** are read when `Settings()` is first called and again on every `WM_SETTINGCHANGE` (coalesced to the next turn of the loop), and arrive as `Handler.OnSettings`:
  - dark mode: the registry value `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize\AppsUseLightTheme` (0 is dark); the title bar of every window follows it (§25.4)
  - accent color: `DwmGetColorizationColor`
  - high contrast: `SystemParametersInfoW(SPI_GETHIGHCONTRAST)` with `HCF_HIGHCONTRASTON`
  - the text scale: `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Accessibility\TextScaleFactor` (a percentage; 100 when the value is absent). The Windows scale (DPI) is separate and is the window's scale (§25.4)
  - reduced motion: `SPI_GETCLIENTAREAANIMATION` false
  - the locales: `GetUserPreferredUILanguages(MUI_LANGUAGE_NAME)`, as BCP 47 tags; the 24-hour clock: `GetLocaleInfoEx(LOCALE_SSHORTTIME)` with an `H`
  - the cursor size: `GetSystemMetrics(SM_CXCURSOR)`; font smoothing: `SPI_GETFONTSMOOTHING` and `SPI_GETFONTSMOOTHINGTYPE` (ClearType is subpixel, with the orientation of `SPI_GETFONTSMOOTHINGORIENTATION`); the interface font: `lfMessageFont` of `SPI_GETNONCLIENTMETRICS` (Segoe UI 9 pt), and the monospace font Consolas 11 pt
  - the caret blink time (`GetCaretBlinkTime`; `INFINITE` is no blinking) and the double-click time (`GetDoubleClickTime`): they are kept in `Settings` (`CaretBlinkTime`, `DoubleClickTime`, a deviation recorded in §12.10 by step 28.6); the caret of `EditableText` blinks at that rate, and the double-tap timeout of the gestures stays Flutter's 300 ms
- **Fonts.** The system fonts are in `%WINDIR%\Fonts` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts` (the fonts a user installed), listed by the registry keys `HKLM` and `HKCU\…\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Fonts` (face name to file); go-text reads the files, and DirectWrite is not used. The matcher (`internal/text/winfonts`, plain Go over a list of families and files, so it is tested anywhere) gives the generic families `sans-serif` Segoe UI, `serif` Times New Roman, `monospace` Consolas, `cursive` Segoe Script, and `system-ui` Segoe UI (Segoe UI Variable on Windows 11), and the fallback chain by script and locale: Segoe UI, Segoe UI Emoji (color, COLR) for emoji, Segoe UI Symbol, Microsoft YaHei for Simplified Chinese, Microsoft JhengHei for Traditional Chinese, Yu Gothic and Meiryo for Japanese, Malgun Gothic for Korean, Nirmala UI for the Indic scripts, Leelawadee UI for Thai, Gadugi, Ebrima, Myanmar Text, Javanese Text, Segoe UI Historic, and MS Gothic and SimSun last. The bundled Roboto and Material Icons stay first, as everywhere (§10). Wine has few fonts (Tahoma and a handful of others), so the matcher is tested against lists written for the tests, and the CJK and emoji text is a manual check.
- **Lifecycle.** The platform reports it itself (§13), as Flutter's `WindowsLifecycleManager` does: `Resumed` when a window is visible, not minimized and active; `Inactive` when one is visible and none is active; `Hidden` when every window is minimized or hidden; `Detached` at the end. Hidden stops the frames and the tickers. `WM_QUERYENDSESSION` answers `TRUE` (the app does not hold the shutdown) and `WM_ENDSESSION` with `wParam` `TRUE` reports `Detached` and ends `Run` at once, since Windows allows an app a few seconds: the session cannot be cancelled by the app, so it is not an exit request. `WM_CLOSE` is the window's close request (§25.4).

**Decided in step 28.6.** *Settings.* `settings.go` is plain Go: `settingsInput` is everything the platform reads (with a `Has` flag for a value that may be absent) and `settingsOf` makes the `platform.Settings`; `settings_windows.go` reads it (`readSettings`), answers `Settings()` and handles the changes; the whole input is compared (`reflect.DeepEqual`), so `OnSettings` comes only when something differs. `WM_SETTINGCHANGE` and `WM_DWMCOLORIZATIONCOLORCHANGED` reach the service window and every window of the app (Windows sends them to every top-level window); the first of them in a turn posts one read (`settingChanged`), and the title bar of every window is made light or dark in that read. The values: dark when `AppsUseLightTheme` is 0 and light when the value is absent; the accent color is the colorization color made opaque; the text scale is `TextScaleFactor` (a percentage) cut to 100 to 225 and divided by 100, 1 when absent or 0; reduced motion is `SPI_GETCLIENTAREAANIMATION` false when the call worked; the locales are `ui.ParseLocale` of each preferred UI language (en-US when there are none); the 24-hour clock is an `H` in `LOCALE_SSHORTTIME`; the cursor size is `SM_CXCURSOR` (32 when it says 0); `FontAntialiasing` is none, gray (standard smoothing) or sub-pixel (ClearType) from `SPI_GETFONTSMOOTHING` and `SPI_GETFONTSMOOTHINGTYPE`; the interface font is the face of `lfMessageFont` with the size `|lfHeight| × 72 / DPI` of the primary monitor, rounded to points (Segoe UI 9 when the call fails), and the monospace font is Consolas 11. Not read: the orientation of ClearType (`platform.Settings` has no field for it), bold text (Windows has no such setting) and whether a screen reader runs (step 28.13). The registry is read with `RegGetValueW`; Wine's prefix has none of these values, so the Wine tests write them with `RegSetKeyValueW` into the private prefix and delete them at the end. *Caret blink and double click.* `platform.Settings`, `ui.PlatformConfiguration` and `PlatformDispatcher` get `CaretBlinkTime` and `DoubleClickTime` (`time.Duration`; 0 is "the platform does not say" and the framework keeps 500 ms; `ui.CaretBlinkNever` is `INFINITE`). `EditableTextState` reads the period when the caret starts to blink and at each tick: a change of the setting starts the blinking again with the new period at the next tick, and a system that does not blink keeps the caret on, with the timer still ticking every 500 ms only to see the setting come back (an app that is idle with a focused field wakes twice a second, as with a blinking caret). `CursorBlinkInterval` returns the period. The double-tap timeout of the gestures stays Flutter's 300 ms; the double-click time is available to the app through the dispatcher. *Fonts.* `internal/text/winfonts` is plain Go. `Scan` reads the faces of a list of files with go-text (the preferred family of the name table, so Segoe UI Semibold is a weight of Segoe UI, and the weight and slant of the OS/2 table), eight files at a time, and keeps what it read in a JSON file in `os.UserCacheDir()\glutter\fonts\windows-faces.json` (keyed by path, size and modification time; a damaged file is an empty cache). This is not go-text's `fontscan` index: `fontscan` scans fixed directories only, and the registry of Windows (and of Wine, where every font of the host is a `Z:\…` path) names files in other places. `fonts_windows.go` lists the files: the values of `HKLM` and `HKCU` `…\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Fonts` (a relative path is in `%WINDIR%\Fonts`; the values starting with `@` repeat a file for vertical writing), then the files of `%WINDIR%\Fonts` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts`, each file once without regard to case, only `.ttf`, `.otf`, `.ttc` and `.otc`. The matcher answers `Match` with the nearest face of the family (CSS Fonts 3, as `androidfonts`), and for a generic family the families of the fallback chain after it, the ones written for the language first (`zh-Hans`, `zh-Hant`, `ja`, `ko`; the request's language, else the first language of the user); `Fallback` tries the family of the request, then Segoe UI Emoji for an emoji, then the chain, asking the cmap of the nearest face of each family; the chain ends with the stand-ins Arial, Tahoma, Liberation Sans and DejaVu Sans, which Windows has (Arial, Tahoma) or a Wine prefix has (Liberation Sans has Latin, Greek, Cyrillic and Hebrew), so that a machine without Segoe UI still has a font for those scripts; there is no last tier over all the fonts (that would read the cmap of every font file on a miss). The generic names are the first installed of: sans-serif Segoe UI, Arial, Tahoma, Liberation Sans, DejaVu Sans; serif Times New Roman, Georgia, Liberation Serif, DejaVu Serif; monospace Consolas, Courier New, Liberation Mono, DejaVu Sans Mono; cursive Segoe Script, Comic Sans MS; fantasy Impact, Segoe UI; system-ui Segoe UI Variable Text, Segoe UI Variable, Segoe UI, Arial, Tahoma; math Cambria Math, Segoe UI Symbol, Segoe UI; emoji Segoe UI Emoji. The first of each is the font of Windows (§25.8 above), the ones after it are stand-ins for a machine that lacks it (Wine, a Windows Server Core); Windows 11 has the variable system font and Windows 10 does not, and the first installed one is used. The names that stand for another family (`Aliaser`): Helvetica and Helvetica Neue for Arial, Times for Times New Roman, Courier for Courier New, MS Shell Dlg for Microsoft Sans Serif or Tahoma, and `-apple-system`, BlinkMacSystemFont, San Francisco and SF Pro Text for Segoe UI. A family that is not installed gives no font and no error. When no font can be read, `engine.SystemFontMatcher` returns a matcher with no system fonts (as before) and logs why. The prefix of Wine here has Liberation Sans in `%WINDIR%\Fonts` and the host's fonts in its registry, but no Tahoma, Segoe UI or Consolas: the Wine test finds Liberation Sans and a generic family through the stand-ins, and the chain (CJK, emoji, Indic scripts, Thai) is tested over lists of faces written for the tests as a stock Windows 10 and 11 have them, with a fake cmap. *Lifecycle.* `lifecycle.go` is the table (`lifecycleOf`): Detached when the app ends; Hidden when no window is visible and not minimized; Resumed when one is active; Inactive otherwise. `lifecycleChanged` posts one update for the turn (a switch from one window to another deactivates one before it activates the other), at the first show, `SetHidden`, `WM_SIZE`, `WM_SHOWWINDOW`, `WM_ACTIVATE` and the destroy of a window; the tracker reports a change only, and does not report a first Hidden, since a platform with no window shown yet has not left its start state (the frames of the first window must not be stopped). The engine uses the platform's lifecycle from its first report on (`platformLifecycle`). `WM_QUERYENDSESSION` is answered 1 by every window and the service window; `WM_ENDSESSION` with `wParam` non-zero reports Detached at once, ends `Run` and is not a close request; one with 0 (the end was cancelled) changes nothing. `Run` reports Detached when it ends for any other reason. Hidden stops the frames in two places: the platform draws no frame of a window that is minimized or hidden (§25.3), and the scheduler of the framework stops its frames and tickers at the state Hidden. *Self-capture.* `GLUTTER_SCREENSHOT` is given to `os.Create` as it is: `C:\x.png`, `C:/x.png` and, under Wine, `Z:\tmp\x.png` work, a relative path is relative to the working directory, and the directories of the path are made. *Tests.* Plain Go: `settingsOf` (dark, light, absent, the accent color, high contrast, animations, 24-hour patterns, the cursor size, smoothing, the caret blink time with `INFINITE`), the text scale (absent, 100, 125, 225, above, below), the locales (a script tag, a numeric region, tags that are no language, none), the interface font at 96 and 144 DPI, the lifecycle table and tracker, the list of font files, the matcher over faces written for the tests (the generic families on Windows 10 and 11 and on a machine with only Liberation fonts, the nearest face, aliases, the chain by language, a font for each script, errors), the scan and the cache with the fonts that Material bundles, and the blink of `EditableText` (the period, never, a change while it runs). Under Wine: `Settings()` read when asked and only then, `AppsUseLightTheme` and `TextScaleFactor` written into the prefix and `WM_SETTINGCHANGE` broadcast give `OnSettings` and the title bar of both windows, twenty messages make one read, a message that changes nothing reports nothing; minimize and restore give Hidden then Resumed (no frame while Hidden), hide and show, two windows, the end of the session and the end of `Run`; `SystemFonts` over the prefix with its cache file, the matcher through the engine into a `text.Collection` that loads a face; `GLUTTER_SCREENSHOT` in five forms and with a delay (`examples/counter`, five runs of the program).

### 25.9 Services

Flutter has no counterpart (its apps use plugins). Package `desktop` reaches the Windows services as it reaches Android's (§24.11): the platform offers `platform.DesktopProvider`, the engine passes it to the dispatcher as `PlatformService("desktop")`, and `services.connect` fails with `DBusUnavailableOnWindows`, so D-Bus is never tried and the tray and the file dialogs end in their own tags when the platform lacks them. The Windows value implements the interface of Android's `Desktop` (open URI, show and close a notification) and the optional interfaces for a tray and for file dialogs, which package `desktop` finds by type assertion (`platform.TrayHost` and `platform.FileDialogHost`, below). The calls that wait for the user run on a goroutine of their own on a locked OS thread with `CoInitializeEx(COINIT_APARTMENTTHREADED)` (§6.3 rule 12); results and callbacks are posted to the UI thread with the same guard as on Linux.

- **Tray.** `Shell_NotifyIconW` (`NIM_ADD`, `NIM_MODIFY`, `NIM_DELETE`, `NIM_SETVERSION` with `NOTIFYICON_VERSION_4`) with the service window as the owner, a `uID`, and a callback message of the platform's own. The icon is an `HICON` made from the `ui.WindowIcon` (the picture nearest to `SM_CXSMICON` at the DPI of the primary monitor), the tooltip is `szTip` (127 characters at most, cut with an ellipsis), and the status "needs attention" has no counterpart. A click is `NIN_SELECT` or `NIN_KEYSELECT` (`OnActivate`), the middle click `WM_MBUTTONUP` (secondary activate), and `WM_CONTEXTMENU` opens the menu. The menu is a popup menu (`CreatePopupMenu`, `InsertMenuItemW`: strings, separators, checked and disabled items, submenus) built from the model of the `SystemTray` widget; a `&` of a label is doubled, since a single one marks a mnemonic. It is shown with `SetForegroundWindow(service)`, `TrackPopupMenuEx(TPM_RETURNCMD | TPM_NONOTIFY | TPM_RIGHTBUTTON)` and `PostMessageW(WM_NULL)` afterwards (Windows closes the menu when the user clicks elsewhere only if the app does this), and the item's function is posted to the UI thread. The menu is a modal loop (§25.3). When Explorer restarts, the registered message `TaskbarCreated` makes the platform add the icon again. A rebuild gives the tray a new model, and `NIM_MODIFY` is sent only for what differs. An app has one tray (`TrayDuplicate`); an icon that cannot be added is `TrayRegisterFailed`. Popup menus are light whatever the system's mode is: the dark ones need undocumented calls.
- **Notifications are tray balloons** (`NIF_INFO`), in 1.8. A toast made through WinRT (`ToastNotificationManager`) would have buttons and a place in the notification center, but it needs an AppUserModelID registered with a Start-menu shortcut and a COM activator for its buttons, and nothing of it can be tested under Wine; the balloons need none of that, work the same under Wine, and Windows 10 and 11 show a balloon as a toast. The decision is §21's, and the balloons stay as the fallback if it is ever made. A balloon belongs to a notification icon: the app's tray icon if it has one, otherwise a hidden one of its own (`NIS_HIDDEN`, with the app's icon) that lives as long as a notification is shown (step 28.11 checks on Windows 10 and 11 that a hidden icon shows its balloon, and else shows the icon for the time of the notification). The title is `szInfoTitle` (63 characters) and the body `szInfo` (255), cut with an ellipsis; the body's markup is stripped (`BodyMarkup`, as the web does, §23.7); `Urgency` is the icon (`NIIF_INFO`, `NIIF_WARNING` for Critical, `NIIF_NOSOUND` for Low); `Icon` is the large balloon icon. Windows shows one balloon at a time and ignores the time-out that the app asks for (it follows the system's setting), so notifications wait in a queue in the platform, a `ReplacesID` of the one shown replaces it in place and of a queued one replaces it in the queue. **Actions:** a balloon has no buttons, so only the action `"default"` exists, a click (`NIN_BALLOONUSERCLICK` is `OnAction("default")`); the other actions are not shown, as on the web (§23.7). **Closes:** `NIN_BALLOONTIMEOUT` is `NotificationClosedExpired`, `NIN_BALLOONHIDE` after a click `NotificationClosedDismissed`, and `CloseNotification` hides it (`NotificationClosedByApp`). When Focus Assist or "Do not disturb" hides the balloon, the app is not told. A failed `NIM_MODIFY` is `WindowsBalloonFailed`, and an app with no way to show one is `NotificationsUnavailable`.
- **File dialogs** are the common item dialogs, `IFileOpenDialog` and `IFileSaveDialog`, made with `CoCreateInstance` on the dialog thread. `OpenFiles` sets `FOS_FORCEFILESYSTEM | FOS_PATHMUSTEXIST | FOS_FILEMUSTEXIST` and adds `FOS_ALLOWMULTISELECT` for several files and `FOS_PICKFOLDERS` for a directory; the filters are `COMDLG_FILTERSPEC`s (the name and the patterns joined by `;`; the MIME types of a filter have no counterpart), the first one selected, and the chosen one comes back from `GetFileTypeIndex` as `FilesResult.Filter`; `SetTitle`, `SetOkButtonLabel` (the accept label), `SetFolder` (the current folder, from `SHCreateItemFromParsingName`) and `SetFileName` are the options; `SaveFile` adds `FOS_OVERWRITEPROMPT` and the default extension of the first pattern. `SaveFiles` (several names into one folder, which Windows has no dialog for) shows the folder picker and returns the folder joined with each name. `Show(owner)` takes the `HWND` of the window, which `PortalHandle` gives as `win32:<hwnd in hex>` through `platform.PortalHandleProvider`, so package `desktop` asks as it does on Linux. The paths are `IShellItem::GetDisplayName(SIGDN_FILESYSPATH)`. A user who closes the dialog is `HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(ERROR_CANCELLED)`, which is `FilesResult.Cancelled`, not an error; a dialog that cannot be made is `FileChooserUnavailable`, and any other failure `FileChooserFailed`. The dialogs look like Windows' own only with Common Controls version 6 (§25.1).
- **Open URI** is `ShellExecuteExW` (verb `open`) on a worker thread. The validation of Linux runs first (`OpenURIInvalid`), then Windows' own, because `ShellExecute` also starts programs: a scheme of one letter (a drive path such as `C:\…`), `javascript:` and `vbscript:`, and a `file:` URI of an executable type (`.exe`, `.com`, `.bat`, `.cmd`, `.msi`, `.scr`, `.lnk`, `.ps1`, `.vbs`, `.js`, `.wsf`, `.hta`, `.jar`, …) are `OpenURISchemeBlocked`. A URI that has no handler (`SE_ERR_NOASSOC`, `SE_ERR_ASSOCINCOMPLETE`) or a `ShellExecuteEx` that fails is `OpenURIUnavailable` (with the reason).

**Decided in step 28.11.** *Plumbing.* `platform.DesktopProvider` returns `windows.Desktop` (`services.go`, plain Go over `shellAPI`, which `services_windows.go` implements with the Win32 calls and the tests with a fake). It implements `mobile.Services` (`OpenURI`, `ShowNotification`, `CloseNotification`) and the new optional interfaces of `internal/platform/desktopservices.go`: `TrayHost` (`NewTray(TraySpec)` returning a `Tray` with `Update` and `Close`) and `FileDialogHost` (`ShowFileDialog(ctx, FileDialogSpec)`), whose types are plain Go. Package `desktop` takes the value in `servicesOf` as `windowsDesktop` (the interface of Android's `Desktop` plus the two optional ones; Android's services have neither, so one platform is never taken for the other, and `services.android` is left nil when `services.windows` is set); `services.connect` fails with a cause that has the tag `DBusUnavailableOnWindows`. `mobile.NotificationSpec` has a new field `Icon` (the app's `Icon` as given: Windows reads a PNG or JPEG file from it, Android and the web ignore it), and `mobile.URIScheme` is the scheme reader of `OpenURI`'s checks, exported. The tray has no worker goroutine here: `NewTray`, `Update` and `Close` are calls of the `SystemTray` state on the UI thread, as are the messages of the icon, and the callbacks the platform hands to the app are posted to the UI thread (the widget wraps them in `foundation.Guard`, so a panic is `CallbackPanicked`). The calls that wait (`OpenURI`, `ShowFileDialog`) run on `Worker`: a goroutine locked to an OS thread with `CoInitializeEx(COINIT_APARTMENTTHREADED)`, which is kept for the next call (a call made while the others are busy gets a thread of its own; the threads, shared by the process in `comWorkers`, end with it), and the answer of a call is handed over after the call is done and its thread is free for the next one (*Deviation from one thread for each call, found when a flaky Wine test was fixed, on the step 28.13 branch:* Wine's RPC server keeps a pipe endpoint for each COM apartment that registered an interface, which every file dialog does, and never removes it; the server waits on all of them at once, so at the 64th, `WaitForMultipleObjects` fails with `ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`, the server thread ends, and every dialog after it waits for ever; 800 repetitions of the five-dialog test hung after about thirty, and none does with the threads reused); `ShowNotification` and `CloseNotification` are posted to the UI thread (the balloon queue belongs to it) and the call waits for the answer or for `ctx` (`NotificationsUnavailable`), so none of them may be called on the UI thread, which `package desktop` already refuses.

*The tray.* The icon has `uID` 1; the callback message is `WM_APP + 3` on the service window; the service window handles `WM_TIMER` of the modal loop and the registered `TaskbarCreated` (`NIM_ADD` and `NIM_SETVERSION` again for the tray icon and the balloon owner). A shell that refuses `NIM_SETVERSION` leaves the icon on the old messages; the two forms of the message are told apart by the high word of `lParam` (the ID of the icon, never 0, with version 4; 0 without it), so no state is kept. `NIF_SHOWTIP` is always set with the tip. The tip is `Tooltip`, a line break and `TooltipBody`, cut to 127 UTF-16 units with an ellipsis (a surrogate pair is never cut). The status, the attention icon and `OnScroll` have no counterpart; `Passive` stays visible. A click opens the menu when the widget has no `OnActivate` and has a menu, as on Linux. The icon is the picture of the `ui.WindowIcon` nearest to `SM_CXSMICON` at the DPI of the primary monitor, else the icon of the program; the `HICON` is kept until it is replaced or the tray is closed. `NIM_MODIFY` is sent for the icon and for the tip when they differ and for nothing else: the menu is built from the latest model each time it is shown (`buildMenu`, `ShowMenu`: `SetForegroundWindow` on the service window, `TrackPopupMenuEx(TPM_RETURNCMD | TPM_NONOTIFY | TPM_RIGHTBUTTON)` with an 8 ms `SetTimer` for the modal loop, `WM_NULL` afterwards, and `DestroyMenu`). *The menu numbering:* the items are numbered depth first from 1 in the order of the model, a separator and the item of a submenu have a number too, and a hidden item is left out and takes none; an item with children has no function; a check shows only on an item that is checkable or a radio item (`MFT_RADIOCHECK`); the label has each `&` doubled and its NUL dropped. `TrayDuplicate` is made by `package desktop` (the reservation) and by `NewTray` itself; the `HICON` or `NIM_ADD` that fails is `TrayRegisterFailed` with the reason of the shell.

*The balloons.* The owner is the tray's icon, else a hidden icon of the app (`uID` 2, `NIS_HIDDEN`, the icon of the program) that is added at the first balloon and deleted when the queue is empty; that Windows 10 and 11 show the balloon of a hidden icon was not checked (no Windows here): the manual check says it, and if they do not, the icon is shown for the time of a notification (not done). The title is cut to 63 units and the body to 255 with an ellipsis, and a body that is empty is one space, because an empty `szInfo` hides the balloon. The flags are `NIIF_INFO` (`NIIF_WARNING` for Critical, `NIIF_INFO | NIIF_NOSOUND` for Low); an `Icon` that is the path of a PNG or JPEG file (it has a path separator and decodes) is scaled to 32 pixels and is the large icon (`NIIF_USER | NIIF_LARGE_ICON`), and a theme name is ignored. One balloon is shown and the others wait in a queue; `ReplacesID` of the shown one shows the new text in place with the same ID and without calling the `OnClose` of the old, of a queued one replaces it in its place, of an ID that is gone makes a new notification. The end of the shown balloon: `NIN_BALLOONUSERCLICK` calls `OnAction("default")` when the notification has that action and ends it as `NotificationClosedDismissed`; `NIN_BALLOONTIMEOUT` is `NotificationClosedExpired`; `NIN_BALLOONHIDE` is `NotificationClosedDismissed`, except that the echo of a hide or a click the code caused is ignored once (the next hide ends nothing); `CloseNotification` hides it (`NIM_MODIFY` with an empty text) and ends it as `NotificationClosedByApp`; a queued notification closed by the app leaves the queue the same way. Windows ignores the time the app asks for, but the app's `Timeout` ends the balloon (hidden, expired) when it passes, and a balloon with no time-out is ended as expired after 15 seconds when the shell has said nothing, so a shell that never reports (Focus Assist) cannot stop the queue; `Persistent` and `Critical` have no time-out in the spec that reaches the platform (`package desktop` makes it 0), so they are ended after 15 seconds too. A queued notification that the shell refuses later is `OnClose(NotificationClosedUnknown)` and is logged. The tags: the hidden icon that cannot be made or added is `NotificationsUnavailable`, a refused `NIM_MODIFY` `WindowsBalloonFailed` (both with the `reason`).

*The file dialogs.* `runFileDialog` is plain Go over `itemDialog` (the `IFileOpenDialog` or `IFileSaveDialog`, made on the worker thread by `OpenItemDialog`, behind `comDialog` in `filedialog_windows.go`). It adds `FOS_FORCEFILESYSTEM | FOS_PATHMUSTEXIST | FOS_NOCHANGEDIR` to the options the dialog starts with (`FOS_NOCHANGEDIR` keeps the dialog from changing the working directory of the program), `FOS_FILEMUSTEXIST` for opening, `FOS_OVERWRITEPROMPT` for saving, `FOS_PICKFOLDERS` for a folder and for `SaveFiles`. Filters are not applied to folders and to `SaveFiles`. A pattern that is empty is dropped, a `;` inside a pattern is removed, a filter with no patterns is `*.*`, a filter with no name is named by its patterns; the default extension of a saved file is the extension of the first pattern of the first filter when that is `*.` and letters or digits. A setting that Windows refuses (a folder that does not exist, a label) is logged at debug level and skipped. `NotModal` gives the dialog no owner (the owner of a modal dialog is a window of the UI thread, while the dialog runs on the worker thread), `CurrentFile` of `SaveFile` is split into the folder and the name, and `SaveFiles` joins the folder and each name with a backslash. A `ctx` that ends closes the dialog by posting `WM_COMMAND(IDCANCEL)` to the windows of the worker thread, again every 25 ms for up to 3 s (the dialog may not have its window yet), and the call is `FileChooserFailed` with the context's error; `FileChooserFailed` is also made, with the `reason` of the COM failure, for every other failure after the dialog was made, and a dialog that cannot be made is `FileChooserUnavailable`.

*Open URI.* `checkURI` runs in this order: an empty URI, NUL, CR or LF is `OpenURIInvalid`; a URI with no scheme `OpenURIInvalid`; the scheme read as a browser reads it (`mobile.URIScheme`) of one letter, `javascript` or `vbscript` is `OpenURISchemeBlocked`; a `file:` URI whose name (decoded, backslashes read as slashes, with the dots and spaces at its end removed, which Windows ignores) has an executable type is `OpenURISchemeBlocked` (the list is `executableExtensions`: the types of the spec and `.msp`, `.pif`, `.psm1`, `.vbe`, `.jse`, `.wsh`, `.reg`, `.cpl`, `.msc`, `.gadget`, `.application`, `.appref-ms`, `.url`, `.inf`); then any other control character is `OpenURIInvalid`. `ShellExecuteExW` has the verb `open`, `SEE_MASK_NOASYNC | SEE_MASK_FLAG_NO_UI`, `SW_SHOWNORMAL` and no owner window; `SE_ERR_NOASSOC`, `SE_ERR_ASSOCINCOMPLETE` and any other failure are `OpenURIUnavailable` with `reason`, `code` and `hInstApp`; a `ctx` that ends first is `OpenURIUnavailable`, and the worker's late answer is dropped.

*Tests, and what Wine does.* The plain-Go parts are tested on every host with `fakeShell` and `fakeDialog` (`services_fake_test.go`); the Wine tests are in `services_wine_test.go`. The shell is Wine's `explorer.exe /desktop=glutter,800x600`, which the first test that needs the tray starts itself (the tests are run by `scripts/wine-exec.sh`, and a program that is started through `explorer` does not return its output); the thread of each such test joins that desktop (`OpenDesktopW`, `SetThreadDesktop`) before it makes the platform, and is never unlocked, so that it ends with the test. Wine's X driver cannot have threads of one process on two desktops: after a thread had joined the virtual desktop, a window that another test made on the default desktop failed with `BadWindow` and ended the process. So the three tests that join the shell (`TestWineShell...`) run in a process of their own: `TestWineShellServices` starts the test binary again with `GLUTTER_SHELL_CHILD` set, reads its output, and fails unless each of them passed; the child's `TestMain` stops the shell when it ends. The dialogs, the worker threads and the programs that `ShellExecute` starts belong to the process's own desktop, so their tests use a platform on the default desktop; the dialog is found with `FindWindowW("#32770", title)` and closed with `IDCANCEL`. The custom scheme of the open-URI test is written under `HKLM\Software\Classes` of the private prefix (Wine's `HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT` does not read `HKCU\Software\Classes` there) with `RegSetKeyValueW` and removed with `RegDeleteTreeW` when the test ends; the program it starts is the test binary again (`TestWineOpenURIHelper`), which writes the URI it got to a file. What Wine's shell does, and Windows' may not: its tray is a small window at the top left of the desktop, not at the bottom right of a task bar; it accepts `NIM_SETVERSION` 4 and `NIM_ADD` of an icon that exists is refused (as on Windows), so the test of `TaskbarCreated` deletes the icon first; a balloon is a small tooltip-like window by the icon, with the title and the text cut to its size, with no toast, no notification center, no Focus Assist, and a time-out of its own; the file dialogs are Wine's own, with the toolbar and folder tree of Windows 2000 and no Common Controls 6 look. The proofs run the program on that desktop (`scripts/wine-exec.sh explorer /desktop=glutter,1280x800 <exe>` under `scripts/wine-screenshot.sh`), with `GLUTTER_DEV_NOTIFY=1` (the window goes to the tray and a notification shows) and `GLUTTER_DEV_OPEN_FILE=1` (the file dialog opens) of `examples/tray`, which the example reads in debug builds only.

### 25.10 Drag and drop

The widget API is Flutter's (`Draggable`, `DragTarget`) with the platform bridge of §8.11; the Windows side is OLE.

- **Targets.** `OleInitialize` on the UI thread, and `RegisterDragDrop(hwnd, IDropTarget)` for each window (revoked when it closes). `DragEnter`, `DragOver`, `DragLeave` and `Drop` carry the key state, the screen position (`ScreenToClient`, in physical pixels) and the allowed effects; each becomes a `ui.DropEvent`, and the action the framework accepts at that place is the effect that is returned (`DROPEFFECT_COPY`, `DROPEFFECT_MOVE`, `DROPEFFECT_LINK`, none). The data is read from the `IDataObject` (`GetData`, `ReleaseStgMedium`) when the drop happens: `CF_HDROP` (the files), `CF_UNICODETEXT` and `CF_TEXT`, and the URL formats (`UniformResourceLocatorW`, `UniformResourceLocator`), which become the text and the URI list of `ExternalDragData`; the formats on offer are listed while the drag is over the window.
- **Sources.** A `Draggable` with `Export` starts `DoDragDrop(dataObject, dropSource, effects)`. `DoDragDrop` is a modal loop, so the platform calls it from a posted function, after the handler that asked has returned, with the loop's timer running (§25.3); `IDropSource::QueryContinueDrag` ends the drag when the button is released (drop) or Escape is pressed (cancel), and `GiveFeedback` leaves Windows' default cursors (`DRAGDROP_S_USEDEFAULTCURSORS`). The data object offers `CF_UNICODETEXT`, `CF_HDROP` for files, the URL format, and the registered format `application/x-glutter-drag-<pid>-<id>` (as on Wayland and X11, §8.11), by which a drag of this app that comes back to one of its windows is recognised and its `DragTarget`s receive the `Draggable`'s own data. There is no drag image (`IDragSourceHelper` is a later refinement); Windows shows the cursor of the effect. When `DoDragDrop` returns, the platform reports how the drag ended (`OnDragEnd`: accepted when an effect was chosen) and releases the pointer, since the button went up inside OLE's loop.
- The objects (`IDropTarget`, `IDropSource`, `IDataObject`, `IEnumFORMATETC`) are COM objects made in Go (§25.2), in `internal/platform/windows/ole`.
- Without OLE (`OleInitialize` failed) an `Export` is ignored and the drag stays in the window, as on Linux without a data device.

**Decided in step 28.12.** *The files.* `internal/platform/windows/ole` is the COM glue and the models that need no policy: `Env` (the Host and the four interface types; there is one for the process, `ole.Shared`, because the runtime never frees a callback and each `Env` costs 22: a test process makes hundreds of platforms; what depends on a platform, its guard and its log, is the `Runtime` that each object is made with), `Target` (the state machine of an `IDropTarget`: the data object is kept from `DragEnter` to `DragLeave` or `Drop` and released once), `SourceMachine` (the rule of `QueryContinueDrag`), `DataSet` and `FormatEnum` (the data a drag offers and the state of its `IEnumFORMATETC`), the effects and the keys (`effects.go`), the names of the formats (`MIMEOf`, the marker) and `Reader` (a `DataSource` over a foreign `IDataObject`). The policy is `windows/dnd.go` (plain Go): `dropWindow` is the target of a window and `dragRunner` starts and ends the drags, over the conversions of `clipboard.go` (CF_HDROP, UTF-16 text, the file URIs), which are reused, not written again; `drag_windows.go` is the calls (the registration of the windows, the loop, `StartDrag` is in `window_windows.go`). The step listed `formats.go` of the formats model in `ole`: the conversions are in package `windows` because `clipboard.go` owns them and their tags (`ClipboardReadFailed`), and `ole` cannot import `windows`. *Targets.* `NewWindow` registers the window (`RegisterDragDrop`, after the input is set up; a failure is logged and the window takes no drops) and `WM_DESTROY` revokes it, which frees the object. `DragEnter` lists the formats (`EnumFormatEtc` with `DATADIR_GET`, only those on global memory) as types: the files and the URL formats are `text/uri-list`, `CF_UNICODETEXT` is `text/plain;charset=utf-8`, `CF_TEXT` and `CF_OEMTEXT` `text/plain`, `PNG` `image/png`, `HTML Format` `text/html`, another registered format its name, and a standard format that is not known is left out (and `GetClipboardFormatName` is not asked for the numbers below 0xC000: Wine answers `#8` for `CF_DIB`); the marker format is not a type and gives the event its `LocalID`. The actions the framework may choose from are what the source allows, narrowed by the keys as Explorer does (Control copy, Shift move, Control+Shift or Alt link) when the source allows the one asked for; the effect that comes back is the action the framework accepted if the source allows it, else the first of copy, move and link that both allow, else none; `DragOver` answers it again for every move and key change, and a `DragOver` or `DragLeave` with no `DragEnter` before it answers none. The drop reads the data on the UI thread, one format after the other: the text (`CF_UNICODETEXT`, else `CF_TEXT`, else `CF_OEMTEXT`; the ANSI ones read as Latin-1, the code page is not known to the plain-Go code; line breaks become `\n`), the files (`CF_HDROP` as file URIs; a damaged list is logged and left out) and the URL (`UniformResourceLocatorW`, else `UniformResourceLocator`, added to the URIs and, when there is no text, the text). The 5 s limit is checked before each read: a format that would start after the time is skipped; a `GetData` of a source that does not answer cannot be interrupted, as the call is made on the UI thread (a worker thread would need the data object marshaled to it), so only the formats after it are saved. One format is read up to 16 MiB (`DropDataTooLarge`), and only from global memory (`DropMediumUnsupported`). *Sources.* `StartDrag` fails with `DragUnsupported` when OLE objects could not be made or the window is gone, `DragInProgress` while another drag goes on, and `DragNoButton` when no button of the mouse is down (the platform's own state of the mouse); it makes the data (`CF_UNICODETEXT` and `CF_TEXT` for the text, with line breaks as `\r\n`; `CF_HDROP` for the file URIs; the two URL formats for the first URI that is not a file URI; and the registered format `application/x-glutter-drag-<pid>-<id>`), posts the loop and returns. The loop runs `DoDragDrop` with the effects the request allows (none means copy) and the timer of the window going (unless a timer runs already), and the machine ends it: Escape or the platform's cancel cancel it, and the drop happens when all the buttons that started it are up (a drag that starts with no button down drops at once, which `StartDrag` and the posted function check first). The result is the effect the target chose when the loop ended with a drop, and none when it was cancelled, ended on nothing, or failed (a failure is logged); then the mouse of the window is released with a synthesized up (the button went up inside OLE's loop, which had the capture, and the window's `WM_CAPTURECHANGED` may have done it already), and `OnDragEnd` follows. A window that closes during the drag cancels it; the platform closing cancels it too. A drag that returns to one of the app's windows is recognized by its marker: the event has the request's ID as `LocalID` and the framework gives the `DragTarget`s the `Draggable`'s own data; the data object is the app's own, so the target reads the text and the files from it as from any other. *Not done.* No drag image (`IDragSourceHelper`); a drag from touch or pen (they are not the mouse and Windows runs `DoDragDrop` on mouse buttons), which stays in the window; the shell's `CFSTR_FILEDESCRIPTOR` (virtual files, as a mail program drags them) and the other media (`TYMED_ISTREAM`, `TYMED_ISTORAGE`). *Wine.* `DoDragDrop` runs under Wine with the pointer and keys of `SendInput`, from another thread while the UI thread is in the loop, and finds the drop targets of the test process through their windows; the tests use the property `OleDropTargetInterface` that Wine's `RegisterDragDrop` sets to find the target of a window, and call it as a program that drags does, with a data object that the test made; a drop of another process is the manual check. The tests are in `ole/com_windows_test.go` (the objects through their vtables, the reader and its tags), `dnd_wine_test.go` and plain-Go `dnd_test.go`.

### 25.11 Accessibility

Port from `accessibility_bridge_windows.cc`, `flutter_platform_node_delegate_windows.cc`, `shell/platform/common/accessibility_bridge.cc` and the Windows platform nodes of Flutter's `third_party/accessibility` (`ax_platform_node_win.cc`, which maps the semantics to UI Automation properties and patterns, and `ax_fragment_root_win.cc`, the root of the tree).

- **UI Automation** is what Narrator, NVDA and JAWS use. `Services().Accessibility()` is the bridge of `internal/platform/windows/uia`. The first `WM_GETOBJECT` with `lParam` `UiaRootObjectId` (the first ask of a client) turns it on, as Flutter's embedder does with its first `WM_GETOBJECT`: the engine then makes the semantics tree (`PlatformDispatcher.SetSemanticsEnabled(true)`), and the window procedure answers `UiaReturnRawElementProvider(hwnd, wParam, lParam, root)`. It stays on for the life of the process (a client that goes away cannot be told apart cheaply, and `UiaClientsAreListening` is asked before events are raised so that an event nobody listens to costs nothing). MSAA clients (`OBJID_CLIENT`) reach the tree through the UI-Automation-to-MSAA proxy that Windows provides; `IAccessible2` is not implemented.
- **Providers.** The root is the window's `IRawElementProviderFragmentRoot` with `IRawElementProviderSimple` (its host provider is the window's: `UiaHostProviderFromHwnd`); every node of the semantics tree is an `IRawElementProviderFragment` that is also an `IRawElementProviderSimple`, as a COM object made in Go (§25.2). `Navigate` goes to the parent, the first and last child and the siblings; `GetRuntimeId` is `UiaAppendRuntimeId` with the node's number; `BoundingRectangle` is the node's rectangle in screen coordinates (the transforms of the node and its ancestors, then the client origin on the screen, in physical pixels); `SetFocus` is the focus action; `ElementProviderFromPoint` is the hit test of the tree and `GetFocus` the focused node. **The providers declare `ProviderOptions_ServerSideProvider | ProviderOptions_UseComThreading`, so UI Automation calls them on the UI thread, through the message loop of the single-threaded apartment** (§25.3): a provider never touches the framework from another thread, and the UI thread never waits for a client.
- **Properties.** `ControlType` from the role and the flags (button, check box, radio button, edit, slider, text, hyperlink, image, list and list item, group, pane, window, combo box, menu and menu item, tab and tab item, progress bar, header and header item, table, data item), `Name` (the label, else the value or the hint as the AT-SPI2 bridge does), `HelpText` (the tooltip), `AutomationId` (the node's number), `ClassName`, `IsEnabled`, `IsKeyboardFocusable`, `HasKeyboardFocus`, `IsOffscreen`, `IsContentElement`, `IsControlElement`, `ToggleState`, `ExpandCollapseState`, the value and range properties, the live region setting.
- **Patterns** (a node supports a pattern when its flags and actions say so): `Invoke` (tap), `Toggle` (checked or toggled), `Value` (a text field's text: `SetValue` is the set-text action), `RangeValue` (a slider's value: `SetValue` takes a `double`, so it is the assembly thunk of §25.2; the framework is asked to increase or decrease step by step, as on Linux, §8.10), `Scroll` (the scroll actions and the scroll percentages from the node's extents), `Text` (basic: the document range of a text field with `GetText`, the selection, and `Select`, as far as the semantics tree knows the text, with the offsets converted from bytes to UTF-16 units), `ExpandCollapse`, `Selection` and `SelectionItem`.  The custom actions of a node are not exposed (not done).
- **Events** are raised only when `UiaClientsAreListening()`: `UiaRaiseAutomationEvent` for focus changes (`UIA_AutomationFocusChangedEventId`), the live region (`UIA_LiveRegionChangedEventId`) and the opening of a window; `UiaRaiseAutomationPropertyChangedEvent` for name, value, toggle state, range value, enabled and expand state; `UiaRaiseStructureChangedEvent` for children added, removed or reordered; `UIA_Text_TextChangedEventId` and `UIA_Text_TextSelectionChangedEventId` for text fields. Announcements (`SemanticsService.announce`) are not done, as on Android (§24.10).
- **Not done:** `IAccessible2`, the `Table` and `Grid` patterns, `Drag`, `Transform` and `Window` patterns on nodes, annotation and custom properties, text attributes and ranges beyond the document range, and a provider for a second root (an embedded window).

**Decided in step 28.13.** *The model.* `internal/platform/windows/uia` has its own `Model`; `internal/dbus/atspi`'s was not moved. That model speaks AT-SPI2 (its `Change`s are states by number, the properties `accessible-name` and `accessible-description`, text diffs in characters, its roles and states are AT-SPI2's), so sharing it would have meant a neutral vocabulary and a change of every function that reads it, which the step allows only if the behavior stays as it is. The Windows model mirrors one tree per view from `ui.SemanticsUpdate` the same way (parents from the children lists, what the root does not reach is gone), and its changes are the events of UI Automation: a node appeared or went, the children changed (`ChildrenInvalidated`, or `ChildrenReordered` when only the order did), a watched property changed from a value to another (name, help text, enabled, offscreen, toggle state, expand state, value, range value, selected, the scroll percentages), the focus moved, a live region spoke, the text or the caret of a field changed, the first tree of a view arrived (the fragment root's children are invalidated), and an action that waited for a node (below). *Layers.* `model.go`, `props.go`, `patterns.go`, `text.go`, `enable.go` and `core.go` are plain Go and tested on any host: `Core` is the bridge without COM (the model under a lock, the on/off state, the translation of the changes into events through an `EventSink`, of the requests of the patterns into `ui.SemanticsActionEvent`s posted to the UI thread through a `Window`), and `*_windows.go` is the glue: `Env` (the `win32.Host`, the 13 interface types made once per process: 71 callbacks in all, and the three thunks), `Bridge` (the `platform.Accessibility`; `Answer` is the `WM_GETOBJECT` handler; the objects of the nodes, made when they are first asked for and let go with `UiaDisconnectProvider` and `Release` when the node leaves), `elem` (the object of a node and of a fragment root) and `rangeObj` (a text range). A node's object implements every pattern interface and `GetPatternProvider` says which ones the node supports (QueryInterface on a pattern it lacks succeeds, but UI Automation never asks it). The vtable of each interface is built from the names in `vtables.go`, which the layout test checks against `uiautomationcore.h`, with the 129 identifiers and the enumerations. *Threads.* The model is under one lock and a provider reads it, so UI Automation may call a provider from the thread of a client (it does under Wine, directly) as well as through COM's apartment (Windows, for `ProviderOptions_UseComThreading`); every request only posts the action to the UI thread, and no event is raised with the lock held, since raising one can make UI Automation call the providers back. A panic in a method is caught, logged, and answers `E_FAIL`. *Names and types.* `Name` is the label; the root has the window's title; a node with no label has its value, unless a pattern shows the value (a text field, a slider), and then its hint. `HelpText` is the tooltip, else the hint of a node that has a label. `AutomationId` is the identifier the app gave the node, else its number. The control types follow the roles as the browsers map ARIA (a tab is a tab item, a tab bar a tab, a dialog a window, a row and a cell data items, a column header a header item, a landmark a group, a progress bar and a loading spinner a progress bar), and the flags otherwise (text field: edit; slider; link: hyperlink; header: text, with `HeadingLevel`; image; checkable in a mutually exclusive group: radio button; checkable: check box; button or toggled: button; anything with text: text; the rest: group); the root of a view is a pane. A node with no label, value, hint, tooltip, role, flag or action (a container) is not a control element, so Narrator does not stop at it; one with text, an image or a field is content. *Patterns.* `Toggle` for a checked or toggled node that is not a radio button; `SelectionItem` for a radio button and a node with a selected flag (a radio button is selected when it is checked); `Invoke` for a node with the tap action that is not a text field, a slider, a radio button or a toggle; `Selection` for a node whose children have the selected flag (single selection, no selection required); `Value` and `Text` for a text field; `RangeValue` for a slider, a spin button and a progress bar that says its value (read-only without the increase and decrease actions, small change a hundredth of the range at most 1, large change ten times that); `Scroll` for a node with a scroll action; `ExpandCollapse` for a node with the expanded flag or the expand or collapse action. A request on a disabled node is `UIA_E_ELEMENTNOTENABLED`, on a node that is gone `UIA_E_ELEMENTNOTAVAILABLE`, on one that cannot do it `UIA_E_NOTSUPPORTED`. *Actions.* `Invoke`, `Toggle` and `Select` tap; `SetFocus` is the focus action; `Expand` and `Collapse` are the actions of that name; `Scroll` posts one scroll action (a vertical increment is `ScrollUp`, which shows what is further down, as TalkBack's forward does in Flutter; a horizontal increment is `ScrollLeft`; a large amount and a small one are the same action; the action the node lacks, because it is at that end, is skipped); `SetScrollPercent` posts `ScrollToOffset` with the offset worked out from the extents, and only to a node that offers it (the framework does so for a node that allows implicit scrolling); `RangeValue.SetValue` posts one `Increase` or `Decrease` toward the value (a second one before the framework rebuilds would repeat the first, so absolute values are reached in steps, as on Linux); `Value.SetValue` on a field that has the set-text action posts it, and on one that has not (the framework offers it only to the field that has the focus) posts the focus action and keeps the text until an update shows the action, then posts `SetText`. *Text.* The offsets are UTF-16 units; the tree's are bytes of the UTF-8 text, converted both ways (`UTF16Offset`, `ByteOffset`; an offset in the middle of a surrogate pair is the start of the pair). The document range, the selection (one, from the base and extent) and `Select` (the set-selection action) are done; ranges move by character, word (a word is the characters that are not spaces and the spaces after them, as on Linux), line and paragraph (a line ends at a new line, since the tree has no layout), and the units format, page and document are all of the text; `FindText`, `Compare`, `CompareEndpoints`, `MoveEndpointByRange`, `GetText` with a limit (never in the middle of a pair), `GetBoundingRectangles` (the rectangle of the field for a range that is not empty), `GetEnclosingElement` and `GetChildren` (none) answer; `FindAttribute`, `GetAttributeValue`, `RangeFromChild` and `RangeFromPoint` are `UIA_E_NOTSUPPORTED` (`RangeFromPoint`'s argument is a structure of two doubles, which amd64 passes by reference and arm64 in floating registers, and the step has thunks only for plain doubles), `AddToSelection` and `RemoveFromSelection` of a range are `UIA_E_INVALIDOPERATION`. *Geometry.* `BoundingRectangle` is the node's rectangle (the transforms up to the root, whose transform has the device pixel ratio) moved by the position of the client area on the screen, read when asked, since the window moves; the fragment root's is the client area. `ElementProviderFromPoint` takes the point on the screen, subtracts that position and hit-tests from the root (the last children first, hidden nodes skipped). The runtime ID of a node is `UiaAppendRuntimeId` and its number plus one; the fragment root's ends in 0. *On and off.* `Services()` makes the bridge on its first call (the engine calls it before `Run`); the first `WM_GETOBJECT` with `UiaRootObjectId` turns it on (`PlatformDispatcher.SetSemanticsEnabled(true)` through `ScreenReaderChanged`, on the UI thread, inside the window procedure) and is answered with the fragment root of the window (`UiaReturnRawElementProvider`); one before `Start` is not answered; an `OBJID_CLIENT` is left to `DefWindowProc`. `Close` (the engine closing, or the platform's teardown) tells the engine to stop, drops the providers and refuses later asks. The fragment root's host provider is `UiaHostProviderFromHwnd`; `GetPropertyValue` of the root gives nothing but "is a control element" so that the window's own provider fills in the name, the class and the rectangle. *Events.* They are raised after the update has been applied, without the lock, and only if `UiaClientsAreListening` (asked once for an update); a failed raise is logged at debug level (`UIA_E_ELEMENTNOTAVAILABLE` not at all). The provider of an event is made if it did not exist. *Errors.* `WindowsUIAFailed` (metadata `function`, `hwnd`) is made when `UiaReturnRawElementProvider` gives no result and when a provider is asked for after the bridge closed; the test client reports a pattern an element lacks as `COMCallFailed` for `UIA_E_NOTSUPPORTED`. *The test client.* `uia/uiatest` is a client over `CUIAutomation`: the element of a window, `FindAll` with the true condition for the children and the descendants, the properties it can read, the patterns, and a listener with the four kinds of handler (the handler objects are Go COM objects of a `Host` of their own). A method with a `double` goes through `uia/callshim`, a function in assembly (amd64 and arm64) that `SyscallN` calls with the bits of the doubles and that sets the floating register and calls the method; the tests of the thunks use it too, and the pointer arguments of a `callshim.Call` are `uintptrescapes`, since the method may run Go code that moves the stack. *Wine.* Wine 11's `uiautomationcore` calls the providers of the same process directly and gets the tree right (`ElementFromHandle`, `FindAll` over the children, descendants and subtree, `Name`, `ControlType`, `BoundingRectangle`, the focus event of `AddFocusChangedEventHandler`, also when the window is activated) but its client lacks: `IUIAutomationElement::GetCurrentPattern`, `GetCurrentPatternAs`, `GetCurrentPropertyValue`, `GetRuntimeId`, `SetFocus` and the typed getters (`IsEnabled`, `HelpText`, `AutomationId`, `ClassName`, `FrameworkId`, `IsOffscreen`, `HasKeyboardFocus`, `IsControlElement`, `ProcessId`, `NativeWindowHandle`), `IUIAutomation::get_ControlViewWalker`, `get_ContentViewWalker`, `get_RawViewWalker`, `ElementFromPoint`, `CompareElements`, `AddPropertyChangedEventHandler` and `AddStructureChangedEventHandler` (all `E_NOTIMPL`); `AddAutomationEventHandler` takes `Text_TextChanged` and `LiveRegionChanged` but delivers nothing, and the next `UiaRaiseAutomationEvent` on the UI thread then blocks while the client makes its next call (a deadlock inside Wine, found with a goroutine dump: the UI thread in the raise, the client in the next `AddAutomationEventHandler`), so the tests do not subscribe to them; and `GetFocusedElement` answers an element of the window's own provider, not the node the fragment root says has the focus (the focus event is delivered, and `IRawElementProviderFragmentRoot::GetFocus` is tested through its vtable). So the patterns, the properties and `ElementProviderFromPoint` (the three thunks) are driven in `uia/bridge_windows_test.go` through the vtables of the providers, as a client would call them, and the tests that go through the client skip with the message of what Wine lacks. What Wine cannot show is the manual checks of §25.13: Narrator, NVDA and Accessibility Insights, the real COM marshaling of `UseComThreading` between a client process and the app, the property, structure, text and live-region events reaching a client, `Invoke` on the counter's button and the other patterns on `examples/counter` and `examples/gallery` (a client process needs `GetCurrentPattern`), and arm64 (the thunks and the shim build and vet for `windows/arm64`; no machine runs them here).

### 25.12 Framework behavior on Windows

`foundation.DefaultTargetPlatform` is `TargetPlatformWindows` on Windows (`foundation/host_windows.go`), so the framework already takes Flutter's Windows branches: clamping desktop scroll physics with visible scrollbars, the Segoe UI typography, the tap target sizes, the zoom page transitions, the desktop drawer and text selection toolbar, and the drag handles of `ReorderableListView`. What was left out until now and 1.8 ports:
- `DefaultTextEditingShortcuts` and `DefaultTextEditingShortcutMap()` take the Windows map on Windows (`_windowsShortcuts` of `widgets/default_text_editing_shortcuts.dart`: the common and clipboard shortcuts, Page Up and Page Down, Home and End with Shift and Control), step 28.4; the maps of the other platforms stay as §12.10 says.
- The system settings of §25.8 reach `MediaQuery` (the platform brightness, the text scale, high contrast, reduced motion) and the caret blink of `EditableText`.
Cupertino stays out (§2).

### 25.13 Testing and proof

- **Wine is the test runner.** Wine 11 on Fedora runs a Windows binary that Go cross-compiled, and gives the app Direct3D 12 through vkd3d on the host's Vulkan. Facts from the probe of 2026-10-25 (Wine 11.0 staging, Fedora 44):
  - A `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0` program runs under Wine; with a booted prefix it starts in 0.1 to 0.35 s.
  - A new prefix hangs at its first boot when `wine-cms` is not installed (setupapi loops on the missing `mscms.dll`). The workaround is `timeout 20 wine wineboot --init` followed by `wineserver -k`; `wineserver -w` must not be used (`winedevice` stays alive).
  - A window made from Go with `syscall` on a locked OS thread and a `syscall.NewCallback` window procedure is created in about 90 ms on Xvfb, and `WM_CREATE`, `WM_SIZE`, `WM_PAINT`, `WM_ACTIVATE` and `WM_SETFOCUS` arrive.
  - `D3D12CreateDevice` works at feature levels 11_0 and 11_1 and fails at 12_0 and above (lavapipe and RADV alike); `D3D12GetDebugInterface` fails (`DXGI_ERROR_SDK_COMPONENT_MISSING`); the DXGI adapter has a made-up name.
  - A swap chain for an `HWND` (`CreateSwapChainForHwnd`, two buffers, `R8G8B8A8_UNORM`) presents on Xvfb **with lavapipe only**; with RADV the device works offscreen but presentation fails on Xvfb (no DRI3). Render targets and read-back work with both.
  - `D3DCompile` (`d3dcompiler_47` in Wine, built on vkd3d-shader) compiles `vs_5_1` and `ps_5_1` to DXBC in under 1 ms; root signatures and pipeline state objects can be made; a triangle drawn and read back has exact pixels.
  - Ten of ten runs passed; the first verified frame came 0.27 to 0.30 s after the start.
- **`scripts/wine-exec.sh`** is the runner for `go test -exec`: it starts a headless Xvfb (`scripts/headless-x11.sh`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` unset), uses a private `WINEPREFIX` (`.wine-test/prefix` at the module root, git-ignored like `.android-test/`; `GLUTTER_WINEPREFIX` overrides it), sets `WINEDLLOVERRIDES="mscoree,mshtml="` (no Mono or Gecko prompt), `WINEDEBUG=-all` (`GLUTTER_WINEDEBUG` overrides it), `ulimit -c 1` (a crash never reaches the system's crash reporter), `VK_DRIVER_FILES` pointing at lavapipe's ICD (so presentation works), runs the program under `timeout -k`, and ends with `wineserver -k`. When `wine-cms` is not installed it does the first-boot workaround above, once, under a lock. The tests of different packages share the prefix and the server, so Wine tests run one package at a time (`-p 1`).
- **Three kinds of test**, each with its own command:
  - *Unit tests of the packages that build for Windows* (the `win32` helpers, COM objects, the plain-Go models): `scripts/test-windows.sh`, which runs `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go test -exec "$PWD/scripts/wine-exec.sh" -p 1` over every package that has Windows files (not `cmd/` and not the host-side `internal/winetest`), like `scripts/test-wasm.sh`. A standard check from step 28.1.
  - ***Wine tests*** (`-tags glutter_wine`): tests that need a window, input or the GPU, run inside Wine: `GOOS=windows go test -tags glutter_wine -exec "$PWD/scripts/wine-exec.sh" -p 1 <packages>`. Host-side tests that start Wine themselves (`internal/winetest`, `cmd/glutter-windows`, `examples`) are run natively with `go test -tags glutter_wine -p 1 <packages>`; they use `internal/winetest`, which makes the prefix, starts Xvfb and Wine in their own process groups under `timeout -k`, stops them, and fails the package's tests when anything it started is left (`Leftovers` reads `/proc`, as `internal/androidtest` does).
  - *Layout tests* of the Win32 and COM mirrors need only the mingw-w64 compiler (§25.2).
  Under Wine the Direct3D 12 parity tests compare `d3d12` against `soft` over every proof scene within `gputest.ProofTolerances`, as `internal/gpu/vulkan/parity_display_test.go` does for Vulkan.
- **Decided in step 28.1.** `scripts/wine-exec.sh <exe> [args]` starts itself again inside `scripts/headless-x11.sh` (the marker `GLUTTER_WINE_INSIDE=1` says that an X server is there), makes the prefix on the first run under `flock` on `<prefix>.lock` (`timeout -k 5 20 wine64 wineboot --init`, then `wineserver -k`, whether or not `wine-cms` is installed), runs the program under `timeout -k 10 ${GLUTTER_WINE_TIMEOUT:-600}` and ends with `wineserver -k` from a trap; it exits 69 when Wine or Xvfb is missing. `scripts/wine-screenshot.sh <file.png> -- <command...>` runs the command inside the X server with that marker, waits `GLUTTER_SHOT_DELAY` seconds (3), saves the root window with `import -window root`, and stops the command (status 1 when it ended before the capture). `scripts/test-windows.sh` lists the packages with `go list` for `GOOS=windows`: a package is run when one of its Go files (tests included) is named `*_windows*.go` or has a build constraint that names `windows`, except `cmd/...` and `internal/winetest`; with arguments it runs those instead. `internal/winetest` is `Harness` (`New`, `Environment`, `EnsurePrefix`, `Run`, `Stop`) with a `Runner` that a test replaces to see the command lines, `Leftovers(root)` (the processes whose environment has `WINEPREFIX=<prefix>`), and, on Windows, `UnderWine()` (`wine_get_version` in `ntdll.dll`). `Run` starts `sh -c 'ulimit -c 1; exec "$@"' sh timeout -k 10s <n>s scripts/headless-x11.sh -- wine64 <exe> <args>` in a process group of its own and runs `wineserver -k` afterwards, also when the context ends the run; a non-zero exit code (124 for the timeout) is in the `Result`, not an error. The tests that need a window or the GPU carry `glutter_wine`; `errcheck` reads the `windows/amd64` build with that tag (§14.4).
- **Proof method F, Wine capture** (IMPLEMENTATION.md): the app's own self-capture (`GLUTTER_SCREENSHOT`, step 7.4) run under `scripts/wine-exec.sh` or `go run ./cmd/glutter-windows shot`, or, for what lies outside the app's window (the tray, a dialog, several windows), the root window of Xvfb, saved with `scripts/wine-screenshot.sh <file.png> -- <command>` (ImageMagick's `import -window root`).
- **What Wine cannot show** (a manual check on a real Windows 10 or 11 PC, recorded in `docs/MANUAL-CHECKS.md`): the Direct3D 12 debug layer; feature levels above 11_1; the `ID3D12PipelineLibrary`; WARP; the real flip-model present (Wine ignores `FLIP_DISCARD`); the adapter's real name and memory budget (Wine reports a fake "NVIDIA GeForce GTX 470"); a real driver's behavior and a device that is removed; the change of scale between monitors and several monitors; real input methods (Microsoft IME, Pinyin, Korean, the emoji panel, the touch keyboard); touch and pen (`WM_POINTER` messages cannot be made); precision touchpads; DWM (the dark title bar, rounded corners, snap layouts); Narrator, NVDA and JAWS; Windows' notification center, Focus Assist and the tray overflow; the Start menu and SmartScreen; high contrast themes; Windows 11 and Windows on ARM.

**Decided in step 28.2.** The tests of the window and the loop are in `internal/platform/windows` (`wine_windows_test.go`, tag `glutter_wine`, run inside Wine: each test keeps one OS thread from `New` to `Close`); the one that changes the DPI is on the host (`dpi_host_wine_test.go`), because Wine's monitors take their DPI when its server starts: it writes `HKCU\Control Panel\Desktop\LogPixels` with `reg`, stops the server, and runs the Windows test binary (`TestDPIChild`), which prints the scale and the sizes it got (96, 120, 144 and 192 dpi give 1, 1.25, 1.5 and 2). The readback of GDI's output is `GetPixel` on the window's device context (`internal/gpu/gdiwindow`). `examples/counter/wine_test.go` runs the counter's self-capture and compares what it can with the golden: the floating action button and the background are equal to the golden, pixel for pixel, and the text, which is Liberation Sans standing for Segoe UI, only has to be there.

**Decided in step 28.15.**
- *The examples.* `examples/windows_build_test.go` (`TestEveryExampleBuildsForWindows`, skipped by `-short`) builds every example with `wintool.Build` for `amd64` and `arm64` and reads the `.exe` back with `debug/pe`: the machine type, the GUI subsystem and a size over 5 MB. `examples/windows_wine_test.go` (`TestEveryExampleDrawsItsFirstFrameUnderWine`, `glutter_wine`, host side, one example after the other) builds each example as a debug build (so that the checks of `DebugMode` run), starts it under Wine with `GLUTTER_RENDERER=d3d12` (no fallback to `soft` can hide a broken Direct3D 12), `GLUTTER_FRAME_STATS=1` and the self-capture, and asserts: status 0; no `panic:`, `fatal error:` or `goroutine ` in the log; a `first frame presented` line whose `renderer` starts with `d3d12`; and a saved frame with at least 8 different colors in a sample. The self-capture ends the app after its first idle frame, so "waits for the first frame" is "the run ends with status 0 and the line is there"; an app that never drew would run into the test's 5-minute timeout. Each example took 6 to 11 seconds (2 to 3 seconds to the first frame) and about 1 GB of host memory; the whole test, 11 examples, took 83 seconds and lowered `MemAvailable` by 1 GB. Only the editor needed a change: its notes went to `~/.local/share/glutter-editor` because Wine passes the host's `HOME` through; on Windows (`foundation.DefaultTargetPlatform`) it keeps them in `%APPDATA%\glutter-editor`. Every example's header says how to run it on Windows and what Windows lacks for it (nothing for most; the touchpad's inertia for `scrolling` and the `gallery`).
- *Lint.* `GOOS=windows golangci-lint run` (with and without `--build-tags glutter_wine`, for `amd64` and `arm64`) is clean. The Linux-only code moved behind build tags instead of `//nolint`: `internal/engine/gles_renderer.go` is `linux || js` (`rasterCacheAfter`, which the explicit renderer also uses, moved to `explicit_options.go`), `internal/gpu/nativewindow/buffer_linux.go` holds `bufferSize` and `windowBuffer` (the Android mirror and its layout test), and the test hooks `Config.wayland`, `Config.x11` and `Config.connect` of `internal/engine` became one map, `Config.connectors` (key `""` replaces the whole choice of `backends_<goos>.go`, `"wayland"` and `"x11"` replace the two Linux backends), because an unexported field that only Linux code reads is "unused" on Windows. No test was changed except for how it sets the hook.
- *The Android temporary directory.* `androidtool.Build` already removed its `glutter-apk-*` work directory (a deferred `RemoveAll`) on every path that returns, a test now checks that for each program of the build that can fail and for a context that ends. The 117 MB directory of 2026-10-26 was the leftover of a process that did not return: a `go test` binary that was killed (SIGKILL by the memory guard, SIGINT, or the test timeout) never runs its defers. So Build now removes `glutter-apk-*` and `glutter-dex-*` directories of the temporary directory that were last changed more than 2 hours ago at its start (`sweepStaleTempDirs`; a build takes minutes, so a newer directory belongs to a build that still runs), and it deletes the libraries of the work directory once they are in the packed APK, which halves its size while the APK is aligned and signed. `wintool.Build`'s `_glutterwin-*` copy next to the package has the same weakness and was not changed (it is small, and `.gitignore` hides it).
- *`glutter-windows perf`* (`scripts/perf-windows.sh` runs it for the counter, the gallery's home page, an animation, a full rebuild and a scripted navigation; `-m` writes Markdown). It is the design of `glutter-android perf` (§24.13) on Wine and shares `internal/perfstats` with it (the summaries of the frames, the readers of `/proc`, the report tables moved there; `cmd/glutter-android` keeps its own table renderer). It runs only on Linux under Wine (`WindowsPerfUnsupported` on Windows, where Task Manager is the tool: `docs/MANUAL-CHECKS.md`, 28.15). *Size:* the `.exe` of each architecture (default `amd64,arm64`; `amd64` runs). *Cold start:* `-starts` runs (5) with the shader cache of the prefix emptied before each (the directory `glutter\shaders` under each user's `AppData\Local` in the prefix), then as many with the cache that those left; each run is the self-capture, so the app ends at its first frame, and the numbers are the engine's own: `first frame presented since_run` and, with `GLUTTER_FRAME_STATS=1`, the stages `GPU context or device`, `shaders` (built and from-cache counts) and `frame without the above`, plus the whole time of the command (Wine and Xvfb included). *Idle:* the app runs in the background (the harness's run is cancelled to end it), the tool waits until its process shows in `/proc`, lets it settle (8 s), then reads `utime+stime` of every process of the prefix (the processes whose environment has `WINEPREFIX=<prefix>`, without `Xvfb`, the shells and `timeout`) before and after a window (10 s): per process, and summed for the app (the process whose command line holds the `.exe`) and for all of them; the frames the engine logged in the window count too. *Memory:* `VmRSS` and `VmHWM` from `status` and `Pss` from `smaps_rollup`, per process and summed (PSS shares a page among the processes that map it, RSS counts it for each); under Wine the memory is almost all the app's process, because vkd3d's shader compiler and lavapipe's JIT are in it. *Frames:* the app runs 6 s (the time Wine needs for its first frame) plus the window (10 s) plus 1 s, and the `frames` lines that follow the first frame and are at most the window after it (the log's times have a second's resolution) are summed (`perfstats.SummarizeFrames`). `GLUTTER_DEV_EVENTS` is read only by debug builds, so the navigation scenario is a debug build and `perf` refuses the pair of dev events and a release build (`WindowsPerfDevEventsRelease`). The report says on every page that the numbers are Wine's.
- *The manual checks.* `docs/MANUAL-CHECKS.md` has a section for each step 28.2 to 28.14 (28.7, 28.8 and 28.9 have no "Manual checks" line in the plan; their sections come from the checks that their `IMPLEMENTED.md` entries list: Microsoft's compiler's warnings, the debug layer, device removal, WARP, a pipeline library) and 28.15, the sweep on a PC. The file's introduction says that it now also holds the checks of a Windows PC. Their status is pending until the owner answers.

### 25.14 Errors

The tags of Windows (more come with the steps; every one has a route test, §14.4): `Win32CallFailed` (a Win32 function failed; metadata `function`, `code`), `COMCallFailed` (a COM method returned a failed `HRESULT`; `method`, `hresult`), `Win32WindowClassFailed`, `Win32WindowCreateFailed`, `WindowsDPIAwarenessFailed`, `WindowsClipboardFormatUnsupported`, `ClipboardBusy`, `WindowsBalloonFailed`, `DBusUnavailableOnWindows`, `WindowsUIAFailed`, `OleInitFailed` (from step 28.13 `WindowsUIAFailed` is made, in `win32` and `uia`); from step 28.1 also `Win32Cancelled` (the user closed a dialog: `ERROR_CANCELLED`), `GUIDInvalid`, `UTF16EmbeddedNUL`, and the programmer errors `COMNilObject` and `COMInterfaceInvalid`; from step 28.2 also `GDIPresentFailed` and `WindowsDevEventsInvalid`, and `Win32WindowClassFailed`, `Win32WindowCreateFailed`, `WindowsDPIAwarenessFailed` and `OleInitFailed` are made (in `win32`); from step 28.6 also `ClipboardBusy`, `ClipboardReadFailed`, `ClipboardWriteFailed` (the names of Linux; a damaged format on the clipboard, or an image that is not a PNG) and `WindowsClipboardFormatUnsupported` are made, `ClipboardPrimaryUnavailable` and `ClipboardReadTimeout` are used, and `WindowsFontsUnavailable`, `WindowsFontUnreadable`, `WindowsFontCacheWriteFailed` and `WindowsFontsCanceled` are the tags of `internal/text/winfonts`; for the tools `WindowsManifestInvalid`, `WindowsResourceInvalid`, `WindowsIconInvalid` (from step 28.14 made by `internal/wintool`, with `WindowsBuildInvalid` (a build that cannot be done: no package, an unknown architecture, a package that is not one main package or has a `.syso` of its own, a file of the build that cannot be written), `WindowsCommandFailed` (the go command failed; `command`, `output`), `WindowsRunFailed` (the program cannot be started or does not end with status 0; `exitCode`), `WindowsShotFailed`, `WindowsScreenUnsupported`, and `WindowsUsage` of `glutter-windows` itself), from step 28.15 the tags of `glutter-windows perf`: `WindowsPerfBadFormat`, `WindowsPerfBadCount`, `WindowsPerfDevEventsRelease` and `WindowsPerfBadArch` (the flags), `WindowsPerfUnsupported` (not on Wine), `WindowsPerfTempDir`, `WindowsPerfCacheClear`, `WindowsPerfProcRead` (`/proc` cannot be read), `WindowsPerfNoExe`, `WindowsPerfNoProcess`, `WindowsPerfAppDied`, `WindowsPerfNoFrame`, `WindowsPerfInterrupted` and `WindowsPerfWriteFailed` (the report's place), and `PerfWriteFailed` of `internal/perfstats` (its renderer), `WineNotFound`, `WinePrefixFailed`, `WineStartFailed`, `ModuleRootNotFound` (no `go.mod` above the working directory) and, in `layouttest`, `LayoutCompilerMissing`, `LayoutHeaderMissing`, `LayoutMismatch`, `LayoutCompileFailed`, `LayoutCompilerRunFailed`, `LayoutFileFailed`; for the renderer the tags of §9.8. The tags that already exist are used where they mean the same: `LibraryLoadFailed`, `SymbolMissing`, `BackendUnavailable`, `RendererUnknown`, `RendererUnavailable`, `GPUDeviceLost`, `GPUOutOfMemory`, `WindowIconInvalid`, `TrayUnavailable`, `TrayRegisterFailed`, `TrayDuplicate`, `NotificationsUnavailable`, `FileChooserUnavailable`, `FileChooserFailed`, `OpenURIInvalid`, `OpenURISchemeBlocked`, `OpenURIUnavailable`, `ClipboardPrimaryUnavailable`, `ClipboardReadTimeout`, `DragUnsupported`.

## 26. SVG images (1.9)

Glutter draws SVG documents as images (D27). The package `svg` has `flutter_svg`'s widgets, and `internal/svg` holds the parser and the painter. It is plain Go, so it works the same on every platform.

### 26.1 The API (package `svg`)

The names and defaults follow `flutter_svg` (2.x), the package Flutter apps use; the conventions of §12 apply (positional required arguments, an options struct):

- `NewSvgPictureAsset(assetName string, opts ...SvgPictureOpts)`, `NewSvgPictureString(source string, ...)`, `NewSvgPictureMemory(bytes []byte, ...)`, `NewSvgPictureFile(path string, ...)`, `NewSvgPictureNetwork(url string, ...)` (with `Headers`): the widget `SvgPicture`.
- `SvgPictureOpts`:
  - `Width`, `Height` (`Opt[float64]`);
  - `Fit` (`BoxFitContain` by default), `Alignment` (center by default);
  - `MatchTextDirection`;
  - `AllowDrawingOutsideViewBox`, `ClipBehavior` (`ClipHardEdge` by default);
  - `ColorFilter` (`*ui.ColorFilter`);
  - `Theme` (`SvgTheme{CurrentColor, FontSize, XHeight}`, the values of `currentColor`, `em` and `ex`);
  - `PlaceholderBuilder`, `ErrorBuilder`;
  - `SemanticsLabel`, `ExcludeFromSemantics`;
  - `Key`; `SvgPictureAssetOpts` adds `Bundle` (an `AssetBundle`; the default is the binding's) and `Package`, and `SvgPictureNetworkOpts` adds `Headers` (decided in step 29.4).
- Sizing as in `flutter_svg`: the picture's size is the document's `width` and `height`, or its `viewBox`. The widget sizes itself from `Width` and `Height`, the constraints and that size, and fits the picture with `Fit` and `Alignment`.
- Loading:
  - `.asset`, `.file` and `.network` load on a goroutine with a `context.Context` cancelled when the widget leaves the tree (§13). `.string` and `.memory` parse on first build.
  - The parsed picture is cached by its source and theme, so the same icon in a list is parsed once (decided in step 29.4):
    - `svg.Cache` is an LRU with a limit in bytes (`NewCache(CacheOpts{MaximumSizeBytes})`, 16 MiB by default), estimated from the document's nodes;
    - `CacheOf(bc)` returns the cache of the nearest `SvgCacheScope`, or else the binding's own;
    - widgets that load the same source at once share one load, and a failed or cancelled load is not cached.
  - `DefaultSvgTheme` gives the `SvgTheme` of the widgets below it.
  - A document is recorded once at scale 1 and scaled to every box. One with a pattern, a filter, a non-scaling stroke or an SVG image is recorded at the device pixel ratio times its fit scale (rounded up to 1/8, at most 32), with at most 4 pictures per document.
  - The widget parses with the default locale; `ParseOpts.Locale` is for callers of `Parse`.
  - A document that cannot be loaded or parsed shows `ErrorBuilder`'s widget (by default nothing). The error goes to the app's error reporter with the tags of §26.5.
